show_title: Capital Allocators – Inside the Institutional Investment Industry
title: Bill Trenchard - First Round Capital (Manager Meetings, EP.23)
summary:
Bill joined first round after starting five companies and led first round's investments in Uber,
flexport and lending home. But in the venture world, you have these resonating relationships
that go on and on and they become particularly important because the evaluation horizons
are so long. Got to do some really cool investments there, the most notable one being Uber,
which was obviously a fantastic outcome.

thesis: This episode argues that the speaker's entry into the Silicon Valley venture scene was catalyzed by a successful exit to Microsoft, and that their subsequent investment track record includes a billion-dollar return from an Ironport sale to Cisco, alongside a highly successful Uber investment that hooked them.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions selling to Microsoft as the event that brought them to the valley.
claims.quote: So you guys sold to Microsoft that brought you to the valley. Tell me about how things unfolded from there.

claims.claim: The speaker describes their time at Microsoft as a brief stint before moving to another company.
claims.quote: I was at Microsoft a brief stint. Then I went to a company called Adelaab, which this is the peak of the dot com pinnacle.

claims.claim: The speaker made a fantastic return investing in Ironport, which was sold to Cisco for almost a billion dollars.
claims.quote: I made one early investment in a company called Ironport, which is started by two friends of mine, Scott Bannister and Scott Bannister and Scott Weiss. And I was like, I'm never going to get this back. And sure enough, they sold to Cisco for almost a billion dollars that it was like a fantastic return.

claims.claim: The speaker describes their investment in Uber as a notable and fantastic outcome that got them hooked.
claims.quote: Got to do some really cool investments there, the most notable one being Uber, which was obviously a fantastic outcome. And that's what got me hooked was just that I loved the constant inspiration.

numbers.quote: And our average initial investments about $3 million these days.

numbers.what: number of people applying for the partner job
numbers.quote: Over 1,000 people apply for the job.

numbers.what: number of partner meetings per week
numbers.quote: We have two partner meetings a week now, rather than one.

numbers.what: amount of money raised by Adelaab
numbers.quote: We raised a billion dollars, which was a lot of money and unusual amount of money back then.

numbers.what: revenue of the combined company when the speaker left
numbers.quote: But LiveOps, we grew from just a handful of us to about 300 people when I left and 100 million or so in revenue.

numbers.what: price paid for Ironport by Cisco
numbers.quote: And sure enough, they sold to Cisco for almost a billion dollars that it was like a fantastic return.
